Christoph Thiele and I are excited to announce that we have been awarded an ERC Synergy Grant from the European Union. Our six-year grant HALF, which stands for Harmonic Analysis and Lean Formalization, will provide us with €6.4 million of funding, starting in spring 2026.

Our project consists of tackling open problems in harmonic analysis and subsequent formalization of the results in Lean.

The challenges in harmonic analysis are related to finding estimates for multilinear singular integrals (proving that the triangular Hilbert form satisfies singular Brascamp-Lieb estimates), ergodic averages (proving pointwise convergence of ergodic averages for 2 commuting transformations), and nonlinear Fourier analysis (proving a nonlinear analog of Carleson's theorem).

After proving these results, we will formalize them in Lean. We aim for one big formalization project per year for the duration of the project.

Besides the formalization of these projects, we will spend time to ensure that (parts of) these projects are done in a general Mathlib-appropriate manner, and upstream these results to Mathlib. We will also invest resources into writing appropriate automation to ease the formalization burden in analysis, by writing domain-specific tactics. While the envisioned tactics will be inspired by proofs in analysis, we expect that multiple tactics will also be broadly applicable.

If you are looking for a PhD position to join this project, you can still apply here: #job postings > PhD and postdoc positions in Bonn. The deadline for postdoc applications has already passed, but if you're a strong candidate interested in analysis, feel free to still reach out to me. You do not need a background in (harmonic) analysis for these positions.
